'''R4-E1 (Arfour-Eeone)''' is a [[Light]] [[Character]] ([[Droid]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

R4-E1（アーフォー・イーワン）

Card Text

ビークル（乗用クリーチャーは除く）にのみ配備し、戦闘力、回避値、航行速度に＋1。常にビークルに乗っていることができ、その時は人員なしで移動できる。宇宙船用の操縦ドロイドとしての能力はない。[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-1301-25o-SWCA.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''ビークルのコンピュータ操作用ドロイドの一体。製造はインダストリアル・オートマトン社。このユニット、R4-E1はボシェックに付き添っている。無鉄砲で独立心旺盛。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' R4-E1 (Arfour-Eeone). '''Card text:''' Deploy only on a vehicle (except a creature vehicle). Power, maneuver, and landspeed +1. May remain aboard and move the vehicle with no other personnel. Has no astromech capability. '''Lore:''' A vehicle computer droid by Industrial Automaton. This unit, R4-E1, accompanies BoShek. Reckless and fiercely independent.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[R4-E1 (Arfour-Eeone)]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 41, 97. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].

Icons[[Alien]]
'''Talz''' is a [[Light]] [[Character]] ([[Alien]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

タルズ

Card Text

武器が命中した他のキャラクターと同じ位置カードにいれば、その代わりに没収してよい。命中を受けたキャラクターは元にもどされる。「夜間状態」にあるタルズは、戦闘力に＋２。[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-1301-31o-Video.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''マフタックは、帝国が隷属化した星系の内、アルゾックＩＩＩ出身のタルズ人男性である。二対の目の内小さな方は優れた暗視能力を持つ。マフタックはカーベの友人で保護者。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Talz. '''Card text:''' If at the same site as another character just hit by a weapon, may forfeit in that character's place. The hit character is restored. A Talz under nighttime conditions is power +2. '''Lore:''' Muftak is a male Talz from Alzoc III, a system enslaved by the Empire. The smaller pair of eyes gives excellent night vision. Muftak is a friend and protector of Kabe.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Talz]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 41, 100. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].

Icons[[Imperial]] [[Pilot]]
'''Chief Bast''' is a [[Dark]] [[Character]] ([[Imperial]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

バスト隊長

Card Text

戦闘のはじめに、宇宙船に乗っている場合、即座に、他に1名のキャラクターを連れて、同一星系内の位置に、即座に脱出（移送）することができる。ターキンと同じ位置にいる場合、戦闘力＋１。バストが操縦する宇宙船は、戦闘力＋２になる。[[:File:Japanese-Premiere-1301-165o-Video.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]].

Lore

''グランドモフ・ターキンの副官。決して敵を過小評価しない。若い頃に親しんだ狩りによって、狡猾さと忍耐力を身に付けたのだ。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Chief Bast. '''Card text:''' At the start of a battle, if aboard a starship, may immediately evacuate (relocate) with one other character to a site in the same system. Power +1 if at the same site as Tarkin. A starship Bast pilots is power +2. '''Lore:''' Aide to Grand Moff Tarkin. Never underestimates the enemy. Hunting as a youth taught cunning and patience. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese relocates to a site in the same system; the English relocates to a related site.

Notes

The preserved frame shows the Imperial and Pilot icons. Its lower edge is cropped, so it does not establish whether any additional icon is printed below the visible area. Japanese-language printing of [[Chief Bast]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 41, 98. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].

Icons[[Imperial]] [[Warrior]]
'''Colonel Wullf Yularen''' is a [[Dark]] [[Character]] from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

＊ウルフ・ユレイレン大佐

Card Text

ターキン、バスト隊長、ドドンナ将軍と同じ位置にいると、戦闘力＋１。

Lore

''帝国保安局（ＩＳＢ）の将校で、ターキンに情報を流すためにつきそっている。皇帝に無二の忠誠を尽くし、その意を満たすためなら、躊躇無く行動する。リーダー。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Colonel Wullf Yularen. '''Card text:''' Power +1 when at the same location with Tarkin, Chief Bast, and General Dodonna. '''Lore:''' An Imperial Security Bureau (ISB) officer accompanying Tarkin to provide him with information. He devotes unrivaled loyalty to the Emperor and acts without hesitation to fulfill his wishes. Leader. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese card says location where the English says site. The Japanese lists the three characters without an explicit word for “or”; the English says Tarkin, Chief Bast or General Dodonna. The Japanese lore describes Yularen as personally loyal to the Emperor; the English says he is ordered to ensure absolute loyalty to the Emperor.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Colonel Wullf Yularen]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=68s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 1:08. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. Icons[[Imperial]] [[Pilot]] [[Warrior]]
'''Commander Praji''' is a [[Dark]] [[Character]] from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

＊プラージ少佐

Card Text

プラージのいるところでは、Ｃ－３ＰＯとＲ２－Ｄ２は、カードルールの内容を使えない。彼が操縦する宇宙船は、戦闘力＋２。デバステーターに乗っている場合、航行速度＋１となる。

Lore

''戦艦デバステーターで、ベイダーの副官を務めた。ベイダーの命により、タトゥイーンでデス・スターの設計図捜索の指揮を執る。カリダにある帝国宇宙軍アカデミーを優秀な成績で卒業している。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Major Praji. '''Card text:''' Where Praji is present, C-3PO and R2-D2 cannot use their card rules. Any starship he pilots is power +2. When aboard the Devastator, hyperspeed is +1. '''Lore:''' Served as Vader's aide aboard the warship Devastator. On Vader's orders, directed the search for the Death Star plans on Tatooine. Graduated with excellent results from the Imperial Navy Academy on Carida. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese title uses the rank “major” (少佐); the English title uses “commander.” The Japanese text joins C-3PO and R2-D2 with “and,” while the English face uses “or.”

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Commander Praji]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=75s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 1:15. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. [[:File:Japanese-Premiere-Commander-Praji-video.png|Preserved card frame]].

''戦艦デバステーターで、ベイダーの副官を務めた。ベイダーの命により、タトゥイーンでデス・スターの設計図捜索の指揮を執る。カリダにある帝国宇宙軍アカデミーを優秀な成績で卒業している。''

'''Title:''' Major Praji. '''Card text:''' Where Praji is present, C-3PO and R2-D2 cannot use their card rules. Any starship he pilots is power +2. When aboard the Devastator, hyperspeed is +1. '''Lore:''' Served as Vader's aide aboard the warship Devastator. On Vader's orders, directed the search for the Death Star plans on Tatooine. Graduated with excellent results from the Imperial Navy Academy on Carida. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese title uses the rank “major” (少佐); the English title uses “commander.” The Japanese text joins C-3PO and R2-D2 with “and,” while the English face uses “or.”

Title

Card Text

トレヴァッグのいる位置で戦闘を始めるためには、プレイヤーはＸフォース消費しなければならない。Ｘは、そこにある［ダークサイド］アイコンと［ライトサイド］アイコンの数である。ドロイドが、そこにいる場合、このルールは適用されない。

He is in love with M'iiyoom Onith. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese lore says he can track droids by sensing emissions, while the English says his ability to sense droid emanations is limited. '''M'iiyoom Onith''' is a [[Dark]] [[Character]] from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

＊ミーユム・オニス

Card Text

自分の支配フェイズに、Ｘフォース消費して、相手の手札をすべて公開させることができる。Ｘ＝相手の手札の枚数である。その中に反乱軍の男性の単一カード（＊）かエイリアンの男性の単一カード（＊）があれば、それらのカードはすべてロストする。

Lore

''ヘネムスィの女性。連れ合いを儀式的に殺す習慣を持つ。航行税で難癖をつけられ、タトゥイーンに足止めをくらっている。舌鋒は鋭く、その名は「夜の百合」を意味する。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' M'iiyoom Onith. '''Card text:''' During your control phase, you may use X Force to make the opponent reveal their entire hand, where X is the number of cards in that hand. If it contains unique male Rebel or unique male alien cards, all those cards are lost. '''Lore:''' A female H'nemthe, whose kind ritually kills their mates. Held up on Tatooine by an objection over a passage tax. Her tongue is sharp, and her name means “night lily.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese lore describes an objection over a passage tax, while the English calls the tax questionable. The two game texts both cause the specified unique male Rebel and alien cards in the revealed hand to be lost.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[M'iiyoom Onith]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=295s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 4:55. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. Title

コーラー

Card Text

帝国軍、ジャワに配備できる。自分の支配フェイズに、同じ位置にあって行動規制ボルトにコントロールされているドロイドを１体盗むことができる。ドロイドを盗んだなら、行動規制ボルトは所有者の手札に戻る。

Lore

''行動規制ボルトに命令するための携帯装置。コーラーと行動規制ボルトは１対１で対応している。銀河規模で広く使われており、「オーナー」とも呼ばれている。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Caller. '''Card text:''' May deploy on an Imperial or Jawa. During your control phase, you may steal one droid at the same location that is controlled by a [[Restraining Bolt]]. If you steal the droid, the restraining bolt returns to its owner's hand. '''Lore:''' A handheld device for commanding a restraining bolt. A caller and restraining bolt correspond one-to-one. Widely used throughout the galaxy, it is also called an “owner.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese text says the droid must be at the same location; the English says the same site. Japanese lore states a one-to-one correspondence between caller and bolt, while the English says each caller can be keyed to a specific bolt.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Caller (Dark)]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=57s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 0:57. Title

行動規制ボルト

Card Text

任意の位置カード上の好きなドロイドに配備する。そのドロイドは移動できず、カードルールを使用できない。同じ位置に別のドロイドがいれば、自分の支配フェイズに行動規制ボルトを（フォースを消費せずに）そのドロイドへ再配備できる。

Lore

''融合溶接器を使ってドロイドが内包する専用ソケットに固定接続する。ボルトはドロイドの回路を支配し、命令に逆らった場合にはその動きを停止させる。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Behavior-restriction bolt. '''Card text:''' Deploy on any droid you choose at any site card. That droid cannot move or use its game text. If another droid is at the same site, you may redeploy the Restraining Bolt to that droid during your control phase (without using Force). '''Lore:''' Fixed to the special socket built into a droid using a fusion welder. The bolt controls the droid's circuits and stops its movement if it disobeys orders. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese printed text specifies your control phase (支配フェイズ) for the free transfer. The English printed text specifies your deploy phase. Both prevent the affected droid from moving or using its game text, and require the other droid to be at the same site.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=352 Japanese and English printed faces], swccgBoosterBreaks, 5:52. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. ''緊急時に、ブラスト・ドアを閉鎖しロックするためのコントロール・パネル。ルークは、帝国軍を足留めするために、ハンガー・ベイ３２７からパネルを撃った。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Blast Door (protective door) control panel. '''Card text:''' Deploy on your side of the table. May cancel the following cards: [[Into The Garbage Chute, Flyboy]]; [[Narrow Escape]]; [[Blast The Door, Kid!]]; and [[Rebel Barrier]]. '''Lore:''' A control panel used to close and lock blast doors in an emergency. Luke shot the panel from Hangar Bay 327 to delay the Imperial forces. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese card says the named cards can be canceled; the English says it cancels them. The Japanese lore says Luke shot the panel from Hangar Bay 327 to delay the Imperial forces; the English says he destroyed it, locking them out of the bay.

''デス・スターや帝国軍守備隊基地の補給所には、ブラスター収納ラックがある。ブラスター・ライフルやサーマル・デトネーター（高温弾）など、兵士用の装備が立てかけてある。''

Title

恐怖こそ統治原則だ

Card Text

任意の大型艦に配備する。その大型艦が自分の支配する星系にあれば、その同一星系のすべての位置における合計戦闘力が＋１される。

Lore

''「各星域の総督は、今や自分の領界を直接支配している。恐怖によって全銀河を統率することができよう。この宇宙要塞の恐怖で。」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Fear Is the Principle of Rule. '''Card text:''' Deploy on any capital starship. If that capital starship is at a system you control, total power at every location in that same system is increased by 1. '''Lore:''' “The governors of each region now directly control their own territories. Through fear we can govern the entire galaxy. Through fear of this space fortress.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese refers to total power at every location in the same system; the English specifies your total power in battles at related sites. The Japanese lore refers to governing the entire galaxy through fear, while the English refers to keeping local systems in line.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Fear Will Keep Them In Line]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=163s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 2:43. Title

＊ジュリ・ジュース

Card Text

「カンティーナ（酒場）」「モス・アイズリー」「ジャバのセイル・バージ」のいずれかが場に出ている時に使う。好きなエイリアンに配備する。そのエイリアンは、戦闘の際に特殊能力を使えない（カーベに配備したなら、“盗む”こともできなくなる）。このカードをキャンセルするためには、そのエイリアンを上記以外の位置に、自分でビークルを“運転”せずに移動させる必要がある。

Lore

''酒場の定番の飲料。多くの種族に酔わせる効果がある。モス・アイズリーの盗賊カーベやチャドラ＝ファンの好物。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Juri Juice. '''Card text:''' Use when Cantina, Mos Eisley or Jabba's Sail Barge is on the table. Deploy on any alien. That alien cannot use special ability in battle; if deployed on Kabe, she also cannot steal. To cancel this card, the alien must move to a location other than those listed above without personally driving a vehicle. '''Lore:''' A standard cantina beverage that intoxicates many species. A favorite of Kabe, a Mos Eisley thief, and Chadra-Fan. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says to cancel the card by moving the alien to a location other than those listed above; the English says to move that alien to one of those sites. The Japanese lore names Kabe and Chadra-Fan as fans of the drink; the English describes Kabe as a Chadra-Fan thief.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Juri Juice]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=239s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 3:59. Title

＊ルーク？どこにいるの、ルーク！

Card Text

任意のタトゥイーンの位置カードに配備する。反乱軍を１つ選んで対象とする。対象は戦闘力と没収値が－１（対象がルークなら－３）される。没収値が０以下になったならそのカードはロストする。対象がこのカードのいる位置に到着すれば、このカードはキャンセルされる。

Lore

''「わかった、今いくよ、ベルー叔母さん」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Luke? Where are you, Luke! '''Card text:''' Deploy on any Tatooine location card. Choose one Rebel as a target. The target's power and forfeit are reduced by 1, or by 3 if the target is Luke. If its forfeit becomes 0 or less, the card is lost. This card is canceled when the target reaches its location. '''Lore:''' “All right, I'm coming now, Aunt Beru.” '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese permits deployment on a Tatooine location card; the English says a Tatooine site. The Japanese says the target is lost if its forfeit becomes zero or less; the English says it is lost if its forfeit reaches zero.

Luuuuke!]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=292s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 4:52. Title

予期せぬ損傷

Card Text

敵のキャラクターが２名以上、武器が１つ以上配備されている位置での戦闘の開始時に、事故が起こる。運命数を引く。運命数＜その位置の敵キャラクターの人数ならば、その中の１名がロストする（ロストするキャラクターは、敵プレイヤーが選ぶ）。

Lore

''ブラスト・ベストとブラスト・シールド付きヘルメットで完全武装の反乱軍兵士も、手榴弾が弾け、パネルが爆発する戦場では、無事ではいられない。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Unexpected damage. '''Card text:''' At the beginning of a battle at a location where two or more opposing characters and one or more weapons are deployed, an accident occurs. Draw destiny. If destiny is less than the number of opposing characters at that location, one of them is lost; the opposing player chooses which character. '''Lore:''' Even Rebel soldiers fully equipped with blast vests and helmets with blast shields cannot remain unharmed on a battlefield where grenades burst and panels explode. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese refers to a location where opposing characters and weapons are deployed; the English refers to a site where the opponent has those cards. The Japanese title means unexpected damage.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Collateral Damage]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=65s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 1:05. Title

ダーク・ジェダイ登場

Card Text

戦闘の際に、ダーク・ジェダイが１名でもいる時に使用する。１フォース消費して、その他の帝国軍カードの戦闘力を全て２倍にする。

Lore

''暗黒卿の存在は、帝国軍の下級兵士の士気をいやがおうにも高める。「貴様が直々に指揮をとれ、少佐」。''

The Japanese refers to other Imperial cards; the English refers to other Imperials there. The Japanese quotation uses the rank major, while the English uses commander.

Title

ジャワの屍体

Card Text

敵のジャワのいる位置で、２名以上のストームトルーパーがいる時に使う。どのジャワを何名対象にするか宣言して、運命数を引く。運命数＞ターゲットの人数ならば、ターゲットは全員ロストする。

Lore

''Ｒ２－Ｄ２の捜索中、多くのジャワがストームトルーパーに殺された。タスケン・レイダーの仕業に見せるためバンサやガッフィの杖が使われたが、オビ＝ワンの目は欺けなかった。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Jawa corpse. '''Card text:''' Use when two or more stormtroopers are at a location where the opponent has Jawas. Declare which Jawas and how many to target, then draw destiny. If destiny is greater than the number targeted, all targets are lost. '''Lore:''' During the search for R2-D2, many Jawas were killed by stormtroopers. Banthas and gaffi sticks were used to make it look like the work of Tusken Raiders, but Obi-Wan was not deceived. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says to declare which Jawas and how many to target; the English says to target as many Jawas there as desired. The English explicitly says the targeted Jawas are immediately lost; the Japanese does not specify immediately.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Dead Jawa]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=103s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 1:43. '''Elis Helrot''' is a [[Dark]] [[Interrupt]] ([[Used Interrupt]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

エリス・ヘルロット

Card Text

１つの位置にいるキャラクターを、他の位置に移動させることができる（その位置にいるキャラクターなら、何名でも可）。運命数を引いて、エリスが要求した価格を決定する。運命数と同じだけのフォースを消費すれば、輸送してくれる。フォースを消費しなければ、エリスは消える（ロストする）。

Lore

''ギヴィン人のパイロット。宇宙空間の真空にも耐えられるよう体関節を密封できる。スパイスと奴隷をカラウーンへと送る。彼の宇宙船ヒンスラには、特別な改造が施してある。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Elis Helrot. '''Card text:''' You may move characters at one location to another location; any number of characters at that location may go. Draw destiny to determine the price Elis asks. If you use that much Force, he transports them. If you do not use the Force, Elis disappears and is lost. '''Lore:''' A Givin pilot who can seal his body joints to withstand the vacuum of space. He transports spice and enslaved people to Kala'uun. His ship, the Hinthra, has special modifications. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese refers to characters at one location moving to another location; the English specifies your characters and sites. The Japanese says Elis is lost if the Force is not spent; the English describes the player declining transport.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Elis Helrot]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=151s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 2:31. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. Title

Card Text

ターキンが乗船していない場合に使える。ロストしたばかりの大型艦に乗っていた全キャラクター、武器、アイテムは、脱出する（ロストしない）。それらは、好きな惑星上の位置か、自分の大型艦に置きなおす。

Lore

''脱出ポッドは、大半の宇宙船に搭載されている。しかし帝国軍将校にとって、脱出は臆病な行為とされている。「敵の攻撃を分析した結果、極めて危険であると判断いたしました。」''

Title

砂岩嵐

Card Text

「大砂原」「ジャンドランドの荒地」「ベガーズ・キャニオン」「ラーズ家のモイスチャー・ファーム」「ジャワのキャンプ」「モス・アイズリー」で使用する。敵のキャラクターを対象にする。運命数を引く。運命数＞能力値ならば、ターゲットはロストする。

Lore

''２つの太陽のために、タトゥイーンでは前触れもなしに砂嵐が荒れ狂うことがある。強風により、石さえも舞い上がることがある。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Sandstone storm. '''Card text:''' Use at Dune Sea, Jundland Wastes, Beggar's Canyon, Lars' Moisture Farm, Jawa Camp or Mos Eisley. Target an opponent's character. Draw destiny; if destiny is greater than ability, the target is lost. '''Lore:''' Because of its two suns, sandstorms can rage on Tatooine without warning. Strong winds can lift even stones into the air. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese lore describes sandstorms and says they can arise without warning; the English says storms strike with little or no warning.

相手がキャラクターか宇宙船を配備した直後に使用する。１フォース消費すること。そのキャラクターまたは宇宙船は、このターンの間中、戦闘と移動を行うことができない。

'''Imperial Code Cylinder''' is a [[Dark]] [[Interrupt]] ([[Used Interrupt]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

帝国軍コード・シリンダー

Card Text

帝国軍のリーダーが、アクセス・リンクのある位置にいる時に使う。どちらかを選ぶ。１：どちらのリザーブデッキでも、２０秒間見る。デッキをシャッフルしなおす。２：さらにデス・スターの位置にいるなら、「アクセス・リンク」「ガベージ・シュートに飛び込んで！」をキャンセルする。

Lore

''帝国軍将校は、アクセス・リンクを使うためのコード・シリンダーが給付されている。各人の保安レベルに合わせてシリンダーが設定されており、引き出せる情報が異なる。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Imperial Code Cylinder. '''Card text:''' Use when an Imperial leader is at a location with a Scomp link. Choose one: (1) Look at either Reserve Deck for 20 seconds, then reshuffle it. (2) If also at a Death Star location, cancel [[Scomp Link Access]] and [[Into The Garbage Chute, Flyboy]]. '''Lore:''' Imperial officers are issued code cylinders for using Scomp links. Each cylinder is set to its owner's security level, determining what information can be retrieved. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese specifies a location and a Death Star location; the English specifies presence with a Scomp link and a Death Star site. The Japanese lists the two cards to cancel without an explicit “or”; the English says to cancel one or the other. The Japanese says to reshuffle the Reserve Deck; the English says to shuffle, cut and replace it.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Imperial Code Cylinder]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=213s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 3:33. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. Title

帝国軍増援部隊

Card Text

相手の場のカードのキャラクターと宇宙船の数の合計が、自分のよりも多いとき、１フォース消費して運命数を引く。その数の分の「ストームトルーパー」または「タイ・ファイター」をロストデッキから取り戻して再使用できる。

Lore

''帝国軍のストームトルーパーは、１個分隊８～１０名で構成されている。作戦行動を取る場合は、増援部隊から人員を補充するのが、通常の手順である。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Imperial reinforcement unit. '''Card text:''' When the opponent has more characters and starships in play in total than you do, use 1 Force and draw destiny. You may retrieve that number of Stormtroopers or TIE fighters from the Lost Deck for reuse. '''Lore:''' Imperial stormtrooper squads consist of eight to ten soldiers. During operations, the usual procedure is to replenish personnel from reinforcement units. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese connects Stormtroopers and TIE fighters with “or”; the English says “and/or.” The Japanese lore describes replenishing personnel from reinforcement units, while the English says reinforcements are typically held in reserve.

Notes

Title

戦士が位置カード上で単独で防衛している場合、戦闘運命数を１回引くことができる。戦士が「タッグ」ならば、戦闘運命数を２回引くことができる。

Lore

''帝国軍の戦士たちは、通常は分隊単位で行動しているが、全員が近接戦闘の訓練を受けており、追い詰められれば果敢な戦いぶりを示す。''

'''Title:''' A warrior's solitary action. '''Card text:''' If a warrior is defending alone at a location card, you may draw battle destiny once. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese refers to a location card and drawing battle destiny; the English specifies a site and adding battle destiny.

Title

どちらかを選ぶ。１：１フォース消費して、相手のユーズド・デッキを見て、ドロイドがあればすべてロスト・デッキに移動させることができる。２：配備コストと同じだけのフォースを消費して、場に出ている任意のドロイドを１体破壊することができる。

Lore

''トルーパー１１２４、デイヴィン・フェルスは、Ｒ２－Ｄ２とＣ－３ＰＯが脱出ポッドから出る時に落とした部品を発見した。''

'''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says all droids found may be moved, while the English says any droids found may be moved. The Japanese lore calls the object a part; the English identifies it as droid plating.

'''Virtual Modern''' — [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber (V)]] (211_25)
'''Dark Jedi Lightsaber''' is a [[Dark]] [[Weapon]] ([[Character Weapon]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

ダーク・ジェダイ・ライトセーバー

Card Text

Ｘフォース消費して、戦士キャラクターに配備する（Ｘ＝７－戦士の能力値である）。使い方は、以下の２通り。１：ライトセーバーのある位置でのフォース消耗を＋１する。２：Ｘフォース消費して、キャラクターに対して起動する。運命数を２枚引く。運命数＞能力値ならば命中する。

Lore

''多面体の結晶石が光を収束し、切断力を持たせる。長さ１メートルのエネルギー・ビームを発生。ライトセーバーは、ジェダイの騎士が修行の一環として、自分専用のものを作り出す。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Dark Jedi Lightsaber. '''Card text:''' Use X Force to deploy on a warrior character, where X is 7 minus the warrior's ability. It can be used in two ways: (1) Add 1 to the Force drain at the lightsaber's location. (2) Use X Force to fire it at a character. Draw two destiny. The character is hit if destiny is greater than ability. '''Lore:''' Multifaceted crystals focus light to give it cutting power. It produces an energy beam one meter long. A Jedi Knight makes a personal lightsaber as part of training. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese specifies the lightsaber's location for the Force drain; the English says where present. After instructing the player to draw two destiny, the Japanese compares “destiny” with ability, while the English specifies “total destiny.”

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=89s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 1:29. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. [[:File:Japanese-Premiere-Dark-Jedi-Lightsaber-video.png|Preserved card frame]].

'''Virtual Legacy''' — [[Han Seeker (V)]] (1210_84)
'''Han Seeker''' is a [[Dark]] [[Weapon]] ([[Automated Weapon]]) from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

ハン・シーカー

Card Text

１フォース消費して、相手側に配備する。ただし、未踏査の位置カードに限る。自分の支配フェイズに、キャラクターと同様にフォースを消費して移動させることができる。ハン・ソロまたは能力値＜３のエイリアンと同じロケーションについたら、そのうち１枚を選んで、ロストさせる。ハン・シーカーもロストする。

Lore

''軍用リモート。特定の個人や、条件を指定しての追跡をプログラムされている。熱光学センサーできわめて正確に対象を追跡する。宇宙船に潜り込ませることもできる。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Han Seeker. '''Card text:''' Use 1 Force to deploy on the opponent's side, limited to an unexplored location card. During your control phase, it may move like a character by using Force. When it reaches the same location as Han Solo or an alien with ability less than 3, choose one of them to be lost. Han Seeker is also lost. '''Lore:''' A military remote programmed to track specified individuals or targets meeting specified conditions. Heat and optical sensors track targets with great accuracy. It can also be smuggled aboard a starship. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese describes an unexplored location card for deployment, while the English specifies an unoccupied site. The Japanese names Han Solo; the English says Han. The English explicitly says the chosen target is immediately lost, while the Japanese does not specify immediately.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Han Seeker]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE&t=192s Star Wars CCG Japanese Premiere Complete Set], swccgBoosterBreaks, 3 November 2011, 3:12. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261106164955/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qqdS5JpNPiE Internet Archive watch page]. rows.text:
{{Set infobox |name=Premiere (Japanese) |image=Premiere-Japanese-box.png |publisher=[[Decipher]] / [[Takara]] |era=[[:Category:Decipher sets|Decipher]] (1995–2001) |released=April 1997 |cards=324 (162 Light, 162 Dark) |code=GEMP set 1301 |country=Japan |language=Japanese |next=[[A New Hope (Japanese)]] |related=[[Premiere Limited]] · [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] }} '''Premiere (Japanese)''' (基本カード) is the Japanese-language edition of [[Premiere Limited]]. [[Takara]] published it in Japan in April 1997 as スターウォーズコレクションカードゲーム. It has 324 black-border cards, 162 Light Side and 162 Dark Side, 108 of each rarity. Decipher and Takara announced the partnership in December 1996. Steve Stanley, Decipher Senior Vice President and General Counsel, visited Tokyo for Takara's introduction of the set. Takara demonstrated it at the Tokyo Toy Show, 19–23 March 1997, at Tokyo Big Sight. The first three days were trade only. The last two days were open to the public. Takara's gameplay demonstrations had standing room only. Hirohisa Satoh, Jr., President of Takara Ltd., hosted the display. Takara pre-sold more than 80 percent of the print run before street date. Takara was translating the Tournament Kit. Japan was placed in the newly created Ord Mantell region on Decipher's tournament locator. A Japanese champion was expected to compete at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. Takara could not ship the Japanese cards outside Japan. The English Limited set is the 1st expansion of Star Wars CCG. This printing translates that 324-card pool. GEMP loads the Japanese faces as set 1301. English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. Poor translations led Japanese players to prefer the English-language cards. Takara and Decipher ended the partnership after Japanese Premiere, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]], [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]], and the two Japanese two-player games. [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] has a separate Japanese product. Language editions are listed on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. == Packaging == Takara sold 15-card booster packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes. Each pack had 10 commons, 4 uncommons and 1 rare. 60-card starters (MSRP ¥1400) came in 12-deck displays. Each starter had 44 commons (22 per side), 14 uncommons (7 per side), 2 rares (1 per side) and a Japanese rulebook. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-box.png|260px|Japanese booster box]]

''Booster pack'' | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-starter-v2.png|200px|Japanese 60-card starter]]
''60-card starter'' |} [[File:Premiere-Japanese-pack-contents-v3.png|1200px|Japanese Premiere pack and starter contents]] ''15-card pack and 60-card starter contents'' Takara's product page highlighted eight main cards. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-mains.png|1200px|Japanese Premiere main cards]] ''Vader, Tarkin, C-3PO, Han, Leia, Luke, Falcon and Obi-Wan'' == Memorabilia == Takara issued player's guides for the Japanese edition. One guide is a fold-out with a Light Side and Dark Side card line-up. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; vertical-align:top;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Takara-guides-v2.png|280px|Takara Premiere player's guides]]
''Takara player's guides'' | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Takara-guide-spread.jpg|720px|Takara Premiere player's guide fold-out]]
''Player's guide fold-out'' |} == Variants == Every Japanese [[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi (Japanese)|Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was printed on an Effect template instead of Interrupt. There was no corrected run, so it is not counted as a separate misprint. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Help-Me-Obi-Wan-v2.png|320px|Japanese Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi Effect template]] ''[[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi (Japanese)|Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]]: English Interrupt vs Japanese Effect template'' About half of the Japanese [[Corellian Corvette (Japanese)|Corellian Corvette]] copies have a stray mark in the printed title. The mark is part of the print-sheet layout. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Corellian-Corvette-title-mark-v2.png|480px|Japanese Corellian Corvette title mark]] ''[[Corellian Corvette (Japanese)|Corellian Corvette]]: unmarked title and print-sheet mark'' == Other printings == English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Takara-overlabel-packs.png|520px|Takara overlabels on English A New Hope and Dagobah packs]] ''English [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] and [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] packs with Takara overlabels'' The English edition is [[Premiere Limited]]. The Japanese [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] followed in 1997. Japanese-language foil versions of some Premiere cards were packed in [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] and [[Reflections III]]. They belong to those English products. The foil list is on [[Translations of SWCCG#Japanese foils]]. == See also == * [[Japanese Premiere Starter Deck]] * [[Premiere Limited]] * [[Premiere Unlimited]] * [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] * [[A New Hope (Japanese)]] * [[Hoth (Japanese)]] * [[Translations of SWCCG]] * [[Takara]] · [[Decipher]] · [[Star Wars CCG]] * [[1997 Decipher World Championship]] == References == [https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 39–41, 48. {{Set infobox |name=Premiere (Japanese) |image=Premiere-Japanese-box.png |publisher=[[Decipher]] / [[Takara]] |era=[[:Category:Decipher sets|Decipher]] (1995–2001) |released=April 1997 |cards=324 (162 Light, 162 Dark) |code=GEMP set 1301 |country=Japan |language=Japanese |next=[[A New Hope (Japanese)]] |related=[[Premiere Limited]] · [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] }} '''Premiere (Japanese)''' (基本カード) is the Japanese-language edition of [[Premiere Limited]]. [[Takara]] published it in Japan in April 1997 as スターウォーズコレクションカードゲーム. It has 324 black-border cards, 162 Light Side and 162 Dark Side, 108 of each rarity. Decipher and Takara announced the partnership in December 1996. Steve Stanley, Decipher Senior Vice President and General Counsel, visited Tokyo for Takara's introduction of the set. Takara demonstrated it at the Tokyo Toy Show, 19–23 March 1997, at Tokyo Big Sight. The first three days were trade only. The last two days were open to the public. Takara's gameplay demonstrations had standing room only. Hirohisa Satoh, Jr., President of Takara Ltd., hosted the display. Takara pre-sold more than 80 percent of the print run before street date. Takara was translating the Tournament Kit. Japan was placed in the newly created Ord Mantell region on Decipher's tournament locator. A Japanese champion was expected to compete at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. Takara could not ship the Japanese cards outside Japan. The English Limited set is the 1st expansion of Star Wars CCG. This printing translates that 324-card pool. GEMP loads the Japanese faces as set 1301. English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. Poor translations led Japanese players to prefer the English-language cards. Takara and Decipher ended the partnership after Japanese Premiere, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]], [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]], and the two Japanese two-player games. [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] has a separate Japanese product. Language editions are listed on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. == Packaging == Takara sold 15-card booster packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes. Each pack had 10 commons, 4 uncommons and 1 rare. 60-card starters (MSRP ¥1400) came in 12-deck displays. Each starter had 44 commons (22 per side), 14 uncommons (7 per side), 2 rares (1 per side) and a Japanese rulebook. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-box.png|260px|Japanese booster box]]
